source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Brakes, p.5-23

procedures.title: Disc brakes: general description
notes: Four-wheel disc brakes are standard on the 1968 Corvette, as in 1967. Optional heavy-duty disc brakes add new front calipers, shoes, linings and a rear pressure regulator valve, and are used with a vacuum power unit.

Each brake has a fixed caliper, a rotating disc, a splash shield and a mounting bracket (see figures 35 and 36 in the manual). The caliper has 4 pistons and 2 shoes with riveted linings; each piston has a seal and dust boot with a spring in the bore beneath it.

One retaining pin passes through both caliper halves and both shoes; Corvette heavy-duty brakes instead use two retaining cotter pins, one at each end of the caliper. Machined surfaces in the caliper stop the shoes from turning with the disc.
The disc has air vent louvers for cooling and mounts on the front hub; the caliper straddles it and bolts with 2 bolts to a bracket on the steering knuckle.
The Corvette heavy-duty option puts a pressure regulator valve in the rear brake line just below the main cylinder.
Any maintenance or service not covered in the disc section is the same as for Duo-Servo brakes.

procedures.title: Disc brakes: bleeding
steps: Bleed as for Duo-Servo brakes (p.5-3), with the following exceptions.
With pressure equipment, set it to 10-20 lbs. for Corvette.
Remove the rear wheels: each Corvette rear caliper has two bleeder valves (inboard and outboard); front calipers have one.
Tap the caliper with a rawhide mallet while fluid flows to help get a good bleed.
